# Open questions

Decisions for the product owner. Each entry is resolved in place with the decision and its date.
Evidence for every question lives in `docs/research/`.

## Q1. Which Android phone is the development device?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Galaxy S26 Ultra (Snapdragon flagship).**
- **Why it matters:** QVAC only runs inference on physical devices (no emulator). The chip decides speed: Snapdragon/Adreno gets GPU (OpenCL), Google Pixel is forced to CPU at about 1 tok/s with garbled output on GPU. The first milestone's demo quality depends on this.
- **Options:** Snapdragon Samsung flagship (recommended) / mid-range Android / Google Pixel / no Android phone yet.

## Q2. What does the first win include?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Talk, remember, remind, reply through the cage. No wallet in the first win.**
- **Why it matters:** Tether's wallet (WDK) currently can't share the app with QVAC: WDK is stuck on react-native-bare-kit 0.14.5 and QVAC needs 0.16 (`wdk-react-native-core#140`). Putting payments in the first win means fighting that migration first.
- **Options:** Talk, remember, remind and WhatsApp reply through the cage, no wallet (recommended) / same plus USD₮ wallet / Mac-only core and Spanish eval first, phone app second.

## Q3. Repo visibility and license timing
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Apache 2.0 in the repo now; repo stays private until the alpha works and the name is cleared.** Superseded by Q210 to Q213: the repository is public as open source.
- **Why it matters:** The strategy is "Don't trust us, read the code" under Apache 2.0. The repo is private today. Scaffolding writes LICENSE/NOTICE and the README tone.
- **Options:** Apache 2.0 in the repo from day one, stay private until the alpha works, then flip public (recommended) / public from day one / private, license undecided.

## Q4. Install the Android toolchain on the build machine?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Install via Homebrew now (Claude installs JDK 17 + Android Studio; the SDK wizard is finished by hand).** Executed as JDK 17 + Android command-line tools instead of Android Studio, because only ~18 GB of disk was free; no wizard needed.
- **Why it matters:** The Mac has no JDK, Android SDK or Xcode. Without JDK 17 + Android Studio + NDK, nothing native can be built or tested. About 10-15 GB of disk.
- **Options:** Claude installs via Homebrew now (recommended) / install by hand following the checklist / skip, scaffold only what runs on Node.

## Q5. How fast must a turn feel, and what if no model passes?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **≤15 s to the first action on the S26 Ultra and ≥85% correct calls on the es/en eval; if no model passes, shrink/merge steps or pull fine-tuning forward.**
- **Why it matters:** Phone prefill is ~150 tok/s. A pick-then-fill turn on a 4B model can take 30-60 s before an approval sheet appears. This sets the Wave 1 exit gate and what we do if no model meets it.
- **Options:** ≤15 s to first action on the S26 Ultra with ≥85% correct calls, else shrink or merge the steps and pull fine-tuning forward (recommended) / accept up to ~45 s for the alpha / fine-tune before any UI work.

## Q6. Who does the cage defend against in the first win?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Defend against prompt injection and model mistakes now (JS-read biometric key); move approvals to a non-exportable native Keystore key at the wallet wave.**
- **Why it matters:** Against prompt injection and model mistakes, a biometric-gated key read into JS is enough. Against a malicious dependency or compromised JS runtime, approvals need a native, non-exportable Keystore signing key in Kotlin: a second native module in Wave 1.
- **Options:** injection and mistakes now, native hardware key from the wallet wave (recommended) / hardware key from day one / prompt-only approvals.

## Q7. Which calendar does Hermit write to?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Write to the user's own calendar; privacy copy states the honest exception.**
- **Why it matters:** The phone's default calendar usually syncs to Google or Samsung cloud, which would break "only the model download leaves the phone".
- **Options:** the user's own calendar, with an honest exception in the privacy copy (recommended) / a phone-only Hermit calendar / ask per event.

## Q8. Who uses the private alpha?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-08: **Only the development S26 Ultra until the demo works.**
- **Why it matters:** S26 Ultra only means we skip fallbacks, device checks and the second model size. Outside testers need per-device model choice, a "this phone can't run Hermit" path and a distribution channel.
- **Options:** only the development S26 Ultra until the demo works (recommended) / a few friends on flagships via sideload / Play internal testing with mixed phones.

## Q9. A working OpenAI key for image generation
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **A working key, with access to gpt-image-2.6-sunburst and -flare, kept outside the repository.**
- **Why it matters:** The first key returned 401 "Incorrect API key". Nothing in the brand book can be generated until one works.
- **Options:** a new key (recommended) / a key already set up on the machine / run the prompts by hand.

## Q10. Visual direction for the brand
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Quiet craft is the master brand; Deep sea is the dark mode.**
- **Why it matters:** Every asset (logo, icon, UI, social) follows from it; regenerating a full book in another direction doubles the work.
- **Options:** Quiet craft with Deep sea as its dark mode (recommended) / Deep sea / Friendly mascot / Brutalist manifesto. Moodboards for all four: `docs/brand/explorations/moodboard-*.png` (generated 2026-11-09).

## Q11. How visible is the hermit crab?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Full mascot.** `docs/research/mascots.md` compares how other agents use theirs.
- **Why it matters:** Decides whether we build a character system (reference sheet, expressions, animations) or only a mark.
- **Options:** Logo mark plus an occasional character (recommended) / full mascot / abstract shell only.

## Q12. Brand book language
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **English only.**
- **Why it matters:** Sets the master copy, the taglines' primary form and the language of every board.
- **Options:** Bilingual, English master with es-419 alongside (recommended) / Spanish first / English only.

## Q13. Where does the repo live?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Transfer the repo from a personal account to DojoCodingLabs/hermit (stays private).** Superseded by Q210: the public DojoCodingLabs/hermit starts from one clean commit.
- **Why it matters:** The repo belongs in the Dojo Coding org (handle `DojoCodingLabs`, with an s). Today the code is in a private repo on a personal account (only an initial commit). Scaffolding commits and the PR need the final home.
- **Options:** transfer the existing repo to DojoCodingLabs (recommended) / create a fresh DojoCodingLabs/hermit and push / keep it personal and mirror later.

## Q14. Using the QVAC and Tether logos in the signature
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Use all three logos now with a not-affiliated line; Tether's written OK is a blocker before going public.** Superseded by Q211: the logos and the partner line stay at launch.
- **Why it matters:** The signature "Hermit, built by Dojo Coding. Powered by QVAC from Tether" uses all three logos everywhere. QVAC is a Tether trademark filing; Tether publishes no brand kit or "powered by" rules, and secondary sources say commercial logo use needs written permission. The repo is private now, so the risk starts when anything goes public.
- **Options:** use all three now and get Tether's written OK before going public (recommended) / use them everywhere now without asking / text-only for QVAC and Tether until permission.

## Q15. How does the phone download the model?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Hugging Face over HTTPS with a pinned SHA-256; refuse mismatches.**
- **Why it matters:** Wave 0 spike S1 loads a model. QVAC's default registry downloads over a public P2P network where peers see the IP and which model. "Tells no one" needs a clear rule before code is written.
- **Options:** Hugging Face HTTPS with pinned sha256 (recommended) / QVAC P2P registry with disclosure / self-host on a Dojo Coding server.

## Q16. License for the character art
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-09: **Character art CC BY 4.0; logo, wordmark and name reserved as trademarks.**
- **Why it matters:** Scaffolding writes LICENSE and NOTICE. The code is Apache 2.0; the crab art needs its own terms.
- **Options:** CC BY 4.0 for the art, logo and wordmark trademarked (recommended) / all rights reserved / Apache 2.0 like the code.

## Q17. Push the Wave 0 branch and open a PR?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-10: **Push and open a PR to master.**
- **Why it matters:** 11 commits (research, spec, brand book, scaffold, review fixes) sit only on the build machine. Pushing publishes them to DojoCodingLabs/hermit (private) and triggers CI for the first time.
- **Options:** push and open a PR to master (recommended) / push the branch without a PR / keep it local for now.

## Q18. Should the logo become the crab?
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-10: **The reference drawing (`docs/brand/logo/source/reference-drawing.png`, the Quiet craft moodboard crab) is now the logo, traced exactly, and the mascot is built from its pieces.**
- **Why it matters:** The mascot is now an accurate front-view hermit crab drawn from a vector rig. The logo is still the old shell-with-one-eye mark, which reads as a snail and no longer matches. The logo appears on the README, app icon, About screen and brand book.
- **Options:** a simplified crab mark from the rig (shell, eyes, two claws) (recommended) / keep the current shell mark / shell-only spiral mark.

## PRD interview, round 1 (ADR gaps; asked 2026-11-10)

### ADR-012. Web surface and the house stack
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-10: **Static public site on Next.js + Vercel only; no Supabase, accounts, analytics or cookies; the app never calls it.**
- **Why it matters:** Dojo's house stack is Next.js, Supabase and Vercel, but Hermit's promise is "no servers". This decides whether any Dojo-hosted surface exists.
- **Options:** Next.js on Vercel only for a static public site, no Supabase, no analytics (recommended) / no web surface in V1 / Supabase for opt-in services.

### ADR-013. Shipped languages
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-10: **i18n-ready; es-419 (default) and English shipped in V1; brand materials English.**
- **Why it matters:** The spec targets es-419 first; the brand is English only (Q12). Every string agents write depends on it.
- **Options:** i18n-ready, Spanish (es-419) and English in V1 (recommended) / English only in V1 / Spanish only in V1.

### ADR-014. V1 distribution channel
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-10: **Google Play (internal testing then production) plus a signed APK on GitHub Releases with reproducible builds.**
- **Why it matters:** Sideloaded APKs need "Allow restricted settings" for notification access; Play has policy review on notification access and AccessibilityService; open source wants verifiable builds.
- **Options:** Google Play plus signed APK on GitHub releases with reproducible builds (recommended) / sideloaded APK only / Google Play only.

## PRD interview, round 2 (PDR gaps; asked 2026-11-10)

### PDR-007. V1 scope posture
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-11: **V1 = first win + ears and eyes + hands (phone-only full agent); Boost, fine-tuned models, iOS, agent-to-agent in V2.**
- **Why it matters:** Sets what V1 means and how many waves follow the first win.
- **Options:** first win + ears and eyes + hands, Boost/iOS/fine-tune in V2 (recommended) / first win + ears and eyes only / everything including Boost and iOS.

### PDR-008. Money in V1
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-11: **USD₮ via WDK and x402 merchant payments in V1: build the mobile x402 client behind the payments adapter and the cage, spike first.**
- **Why it matters:** WDK is blocked on bare-kit; x402 has no React Native path yet.
- **Options:** USD₮ send with spend limits via WDK, x402 in V2 (recommended) / USD₮ + x402 merchant payments in V1 / no money in V1.

### PDR-009. Model strategy
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-11: **Stock model chosen by the eval; fine-tuning pipeline only if no stock model clears the Q5 bar.**
- **Why it matters:** Decides whether a training pipeline is part of V1.
- **Options:** stock model chosen by the eval, fine-tune only if it misses the bar (recommended) / fine-tuned Hermit models required in V1 / stock only, no fine-tuning in V1.

### PDR-010. Memory portability (changing shells)
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-11: **Phone-to-phone transfer over Holepunch in V1: pairing + transport move into V1, Boost reuses them.**
- **Why it matters:** Data lifecycle: what happens to memories, keys and the log when the user changes phones; Android backup is off.
- **Options:** encrypted export file with a passphrase (recommended) / no portability in V1 / phone-to-phone transfer over Holepunch in V1.

## PRD interview, close (asked 2026-11-11)
- **Status:** resolved 2026-11-11: **Accepted all remaining recommendations (ADR-015, ADR-016, PDR-011 to PDR-016). All 26 decision records Accepted.**
- **Remaining recommendations:** ADR-015 x402 client in a pure-TS payments package (EIP-3009 via the WDK EVM account), spike first; ADR-016 Holepunch transport in the QVAC worklet with QR + 6-digit pairing, shared with Boost; PDR-011 money always asks, with per-payment and daily caps the user sets; PDR-012 the audit log is kept on the device until the user clears it, and clearing is itself logged; PDR-013 accessibility: TalkBack, dynamic type, WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; PDR-014 voice: push-to-talk first, es/en speech in and out on device; PDR-015 web: read-only by default through the quarantined reader, logins only through the vault with exact-origin binding; PDR-016 release bands V1, V2 (Boost, iOS, fine-tuning, agent-to-agent), V3 (Keep watch, Mac powers, family sharing, confidential cloud Boost).
- **Options:** accept the remaining recommendations (recommended) / one more round / show me the list first.

## Parity gaps (logged 2026-11-11, from the competitor parity review; not yet asked)
Gaps found by comparing Hermit's features with Muse, Claude Duet, dots, Grok Bot, Instinct and Atomic Agent. Each answer may supersede PDR-007, PDR-015 or PDR-016.
- **Q19 Email.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Email in V1, direct from the phone** (IMAP/SMTP, Gmail and Outlook APIs, tokens in the vault, send always asks). Every competitor reads, drafts and sends email; the PRD has no email epic. Options: email in V1 via direct IMAP/Gmail API from the phone, tokens in the vault (recommended) / email in V2 / no email.
- **Q20 Acting on websites.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Both: simple known flows on the phone in V1 (on-device browser, step-by-step approval), open-ended browsing on Boost in V2** (supersedes PDR-015). Competitors drive a browser to buy, book and sign in; PDR-015 makes the web read-only. Options: on-device agentic browser for allow-listed tasks, approved step by step, in V1 hands wave (recommended) / acting browser only through Boost in V2 / stay read-only.
- **Q21 Connectors.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Direct connectors plus an MCP client in V1, after research into connector platforms (Composio, aisa.one) and connectors built on the fly (Instinct writes an API integration when no MCP server exists, or offers a vault entry for email and password); see `docs/research/connectors.md`.** Duet 6,000+, dots 4,000+, Muse Connectors; Hermit has ~20 typed skills. Options: direct-from-phone connectors (OAuth tokens in the vault, no Hermit server) for the top services, plus MCP client, in V1 (recommended) / connectors in V2 / typed skills only.
- **Q22 Reaching Hermit and calls.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Hermit is chat-first and voice is secondary. V1 adds voice notes in the chat, transcribed on the phone by QVAC's speech to text. Realtime voice and calls are not in V1** (supersedes PDR-014). Instinct and dots are reachable by text and phone call; Muse has realtime voice and an avatar. Options: hands-free realtime voice conversation on device in V1, phone-call answering in V2 (recommended) / both in V2 / push-to-talk only.

## Connector follow-ups (logged 2026-11-11 from `docs/research/connectors.md`; not yet asked)
- **Q23 Google OAuth client.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Both: Dojo's own client by default (100-user cap in testing, Google verification is a go-live dependency), plus a bring-your-own client option in settings.** Does Hermit ship its own Google OAuth client (Dojo registers it; under 100 users while unverified, then Google verification and possibly the annual security assessment before public), or do users register their own?
- **Q24 Providers that require a client secret.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **All three, layered: default is no relay (MCP server or in-app browser); a user-hosted open-source relay is available in V1; a Dojo-hosted relay that only swaps codes for tokens and stores nothing is offered as an explicit opt-in, open source and disclosed on the privacy screen.** Original: (Slack, Notion, LinkedIn, unverified). Allowed paths: no relay (reach them through MCP servers the user adds or the in-app browser), a token relay the user hosts on Boost, or a Dojo-hosted relay.
- **Q25 Model-drafted connectors in V1.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Yes, in V1** (specs only, never code; non-read operations start at write risk; user approves the spec). Should the "connect to X" flow where the phone model drafts a connector spec from the service's docs (spec only, never code; every non-read operation starts at write risk; the user approves the spec) ship in V1?
- **OQ-06 Google security assessment** (logged 2026-11-11, blocks go-live): does Google's restricted-scope security assessment apply to an on-device Gmail client? A question for Google, not a modal.

## Q28 Where to build the Android dev APK (logged 2026-11-11, blocks W1)
- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Build in GitHub Actions on the private repo; install the APK on the S26 over USB.** Local NDK and Gradle caches can be deleted.
The first native build ran the Mac down to 0.8 GB free (watchdog stopped it). It needs about 5 GB more (CMake, native compile of SQLCipher and QVAC's runtime, React Native outputs) on top of the 3.1 GB NDK and 3.4 GB Gradle caches already used. Options: build in GitHub Actions on the private repo and install the APK over USB (recommended) / free at least 10 GB on the Mac / delete the Gradle caches and NDK now and wait.

## W1 list (found during the spikes, 2026-11-11)
- **expo-notifications ships Firebase messaging and the Play install referrer.** The debug APK declared `c2dm RECEIVE`, `BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE` and a dozen launcher badge permissions. Blocked in `app.json`; still to do in W1: exclude the Firebase and install-referrer libraries from the build (or replace expo-notifications with a local-only alarm module) and add an APK permission check to CI (FR-PRIV-01).
- **Spike S1 passed on the S26 (2026-11-11):** BotPsy-0.8B Q4_K_M loads in 18.7 s with all 25 layers on the GPU (ctx 8192); first action (pick) 7.3 s with first token at 4.5 s; reply 2.5 s; whole turn about 10 s, within the 15 s bar. Prompt 65 to 97 tok/s, decode only about 5 tok/s: investigate the GPU backend (Vulkan vs OpenCL) and thinking/profile settings in the W2 eval.
- **QVAC in a pnpm monorepo:** bundled from apps/mobile, worker keys start with "/../../node_modules" but Bare requests "file:///node_modules", so the worker aborts (CANNOT_READ). `scripts/qvac-bundle.mjs` rebuilds the bundle from the workspace root after prebuild. Worth reporting upstream to Tether.
- **Backend benchmark on the S26 (2026-11-11), BotPsy-0.8B Q4_K_M, "hola":** QVAC default GPU: pick 6.8 s, reply 2.9 s, 6 to 7 tok/s. OpenCL: 4.2 s and 2.3 s, 8 tok/s. Vulkan: grammar-constrained decoding failed (empty grammar stack). **CPU with 8 threads: pick 1.1 s, reply 0.8 s, 21 to 32 tok/s decode, 450 to 500 tok/s prompt.** Pinned CPU8 in the profiles; a whole turn is about 2 s.

## Q29 The model is too weak for the first win (logged 2026-11-11, blocks the W1 gate)
- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Run the model eval now on the phone** (BotPsy-0.8B variants vs Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B, es/en first-win cases, PDR-003 bar).
On the S26, BotPsy-0.8B is fast on CPU (~2 s per turn) but makes basic mistakes: it confused remind/remember/recall, wandered to forget after a failure, invented a passport date, and answered Spanish in English. Guards fixed each case, but a 0.8B model will keep finding new ones. Options: run the W2 model eval now on the phone (BotPsy-0.8B variants vs Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B, 40 es/en cases, decide by PDR-003) (recommended) / switch to Qwen3.5-2B now without the eval / keep BotPsy with guards until W2.

## Harness questions (logged 2026-11-11 from `docs/research/harness-diagnosis.md`)
- **Q30 Thinking on the phone's first action.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Thinking on with a hard budget that closes the think block cleanly, measured on the S26 against the 15 s bar.** On the Mac, BotPsy in its native format scores 31/40 with thinking on (median first action 2.9 s, p90 9.1 s) against 25 to 29/40 with thinking off (about 0.4 s). The phone's CPU is slower than the Mac, so thinking likely means several seconds per action. Options: native format with thinking on and a hard budget that closes the think block cleanly, measured on the S26 against the 15 s bar (recommended) / native format with thinking off, rich descriptions (fast, a few points lower) / keep the current JSON harness until the eval set grows.
- **Q31 Parity gate for the Virtual Assistant vertical.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Per family: no worse than the best competitor on memory, time, messaging and honesty; better than all on privacy families.** A parity gate compares against a named baseline with a margin set in advance. Options: per capability family, no worse than the best competitor on memory, time, messaging and honesty, and better than all on privacy families (recommended) / no worse than the competitor median / no worse than one named competitor (Instinct).
- **Q32 Feedback into evals and training.** RESOLVED 2026-11-11: **Opt-in setting that shares redacted turns automatically** (it needs a privacy-screen disclosure, a redaction spec and a PDR before it ships). Thumbs-down turns could become eval cases (and later fine-tune data, PDR-009). Options: only with explicit per-item consent, stored on the phone, exported by the user (recommended) / never, synthetic data only / opt-in setting that shares redacted turns automatically.
- **W1 list additions (not questions):** count tokens before each call and drop the oldest turns behind a notice (FR-LOOP-07); give every tool call in history a result, including denied ones, before the native format ships in the loop.

## Overnight questions (logged 2026-11-12 from the harness and device-adaptive work; not yet asked)
- **Q33 Phones below the floor.** RESOLVED 2026-11-12: **Both: by default the model is off and reminders, memory and calendar work through forms; the user can choose to run the model anyway, with a warning.** Under 3 GB of RAM, or CPUs without ARMv8.2 dot product (Cortex-A53-only phones), run BotPsy too slowly to be useful. Options: let them install, but turn off the model, keeping reminders, memory and calendar through forms (recommended) / block the install with a clear message / let them run the model anyway with a warning.
- **Q34 A second, small model for routing.** RESOLVED 2026-11-12: **Keep phrase routing; revisit with a larger example bank.** Data (2026-11-12): EmbeddingGemma-300M (334 MB) reached 85 to 92% precision overall, but only 60 to 86% on the cases the phrase router misses (it mistakes "add something" asks for calendar_add). That is below the bar, so the recommendation is now to keep phrase routing and revisit with a larger example bank. The phrase router is precise but can't list every way people talk. A multilingual embedding model (about 120 MB, runs through QVAC) would route by meaning. Character n-gram and BotPsy embeddings measured only 60 to 83% precision. Options: try a multilingual embedding model on the Mac first and ship it only if precision is at least 95% on the blind sets (recommended) / ship it now / keep phrase routing only.
- **Q35 Patch QVAC for an in-memory prompt cache.** RESOLVED 2026-11-12: **Turn the cache on; writing it to disk is accepted.** (It sits in the app's private storage, not encrypted by SQLCipher; it encodes conversation content. Accepted knowingly.) Each step re-reads the 1,000 to 1,500 token prompt, 2 to 3 s on the S26 and far more on cheap phones. QVAC's engine supports memory-only caching (`ephemeral`), but SDK 0.23 always writes the cache to disk unencrypted, which is why it is off. Options: a local `pnpm patch` that passes `ephemeral` and never writes the cache, verified on the S26 that no cache file appears, plus an upstream request to Tether (recommended) / ask Tether and wait / leave caching off.

## Perceived speed (logged 2026-11-12)
- **Q36 Show the model's reasoning while it thinks?** RESOLVED 2026-11-12: **Collapsible "Pensando" panel streaming the live reasoning, closed by default** (plus the instant status line, answer streaming and cosmetics). On the S26 a decision takes 7 to 11 s, mostly BotPsy thinking (up to 256 tokens), so progress should show in real time. Options: a live status line only (instant intent from the router, then the step: "Revisando tu calendario..."), no reasoning text (recommended) / a collapsible "Pensando" panel with the live reasoning, closed by default / show the reasoning streaming in the chat, collapsing when the answer starts.

The research (`docs/research/web-on-phone.md`) found no published sub-1B web navigation result, so open-ended browsing stays on Boost while the research lane works toward the phone.
- **Q38 May a tainted turn (an open web task) run on Boost?** Logged 2026-11-12, blocks V2 Boost web work (US-WEB-10), not V1. US-BOOST-03 says vault, wallet and tainted turns never route to Boost, but an open-ended web task is tainted from its first page, so as written US-WEB-10 can never run. Options: let Boost run tainted web turns as an executor under the phone's cage (Boost never holds vault or wallet secrets, every commit is approved on the phone, page text only reaches the planner as typed records) (recommended) / allow it only on the user's own computer, never the confidential cloud / keep the rule strict and run open web tasks only on the phone once it can (US-WEB-10 waits for PDR-026).
- **Q39 An opt-in cloud path for the hardest requests?** Logged 2026-11-13, not yet asked; blocks nothing today (the SOTA research, `docs/research/harness-sota-parity.md` tip 67). The research found that sending the few requests a small model fails to a large cloud model can match frontier quality at low cost. The trade-off is that it breaks "fully on-device", which is Hermit's core promise. Options to ask, with data on how often requests fail on the phone (Q32 opt-in sharing): no cloud path, Boost on the user's own computer only (recommended) / an explicit per-request opt-in to a cloud model with a redaction preview / an always-on cloud fallback for failed turns.

## Speed (logged 2026-11-14)
- **Q40 V1 scope, to deliver faster?** RESOLVED 2026-11-14: **keep the full V1 scope; go faster by building more slices in parallel.** 47 V1 slices remain (W2 15, W3 13, W4 9, W5 5, W6 5); the cadence estimate is about 32 days. Options:
  - **Core assistant V1 (recommended):** voice notes, the model bar on device, stop and catch-up, download recovery, web reading and search, settings, privacy, accessibility, memory and reminder lists, and distribution. That is 17 slices. Email and connectors, vault and forms, web tasks, wallet and payments, phone transfer and autofill move to V1.1.
  - **Core plus the USD₮ wallet:** the core above, plus the WDK and x402 spikes and W5 (about 24 slices). It keeps the Tether-stack story in V1.
  - **Keep the full V1 scope:** all 47 slices, faster only through parallelism.
- **Q41 How to parallelize the build?** RESOLVED 2026-11-14: **local agents on the build machine**, in separate worktrees, with heavy runs one at a time. Parallel load had crashed the build machine twice. Options:
  - **Cloud agents (recommended):** each slice runs in its own cloud session. The Mac only reviews, merges and runs phone sessions. It costs usage.
  - **Local worktrees, 2 at a time:** safe on this Mac, at about twice the current pace.
  - **A bigger dedicated build machine:** many local agents, but it needs hardware.
- **Q42 Connector reads: ask every time, or once per domain per session?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-47 (PR #40), not yet asked. The risk matrix puts connector reads at `network`, and with today's rules every read asks. An "ask once per domain per session" rule would cut the prompts. Options to ask: once per domain per session (recommended) / every read asks / reads from bundled connectors never ask.
- **Q43 Dojo accounts for connectors.** RESOLVED 2026-11-21: set them up now. Dojo's account owner creates Dojo's Google Cloud and Microsoft Entra apps and the relay host and keeps the signing key off the repository; the step-by-step guide is in the repository, and the values are wired into the app. Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-47; blocks real sign-in, not the code. Needed: a Dojo spec-signing key (Ed25519), Dojo OAuth client IDs (Google first, then Microsoft and Spotify), and the Dojo relay URL (off by default, PDR-022). Guide written 2026-11-21: `docs/build/dojo-accounts-setup.md`; the decisions it needs are Q160 to Q168.
- **Q44 USD₮ on x402 for the W5 gate.** RESOLVED 2026-11-14: **Hermit is USD₮ only.** The W5 gate settles USD₮0, so we self-host a facilitator on a USD₮0 testnet; the Base Sepolia USDC payment only proved the protocol and USDC is never payable (PDR-027). Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-18 (PR #42, `docs/research/x402-spike.md`), not yet asked; blocks the W5 gate, not W2. Hermit's x402 code signs payments that the public testnet facilitator accepts for Base Sepolia USDC. USD₮0 exists on Stable testnet with a verified signing domain, but no public facilitator settles it. Options to ask: self-host a Stable testnet facilitator so the gate uses USD₮0 (recommended, it keeps the Tether stack end to end) / run the W5 gate on Base Sepolia USDC and add USD₮ when a facilitator exists / both.

For the erase, SL-26 accepts the fingerprint or the phone's PIN, and a phone with no lock at all relies on the typed word alone (the screen says so), because the erase only destroys the user's own data and a changed or missing fingerprint must not trap someone who wants to leave (Android's "Clear storage" can erase the app anyway). Options to ask: fingerprint or PIN, typed word alone on a phone with no lock (recommended, built) / strong fingerprint only, like approvals, no erase from the app without one / typed word only, no fingerprint.
- **Q51 Clearing the activity log: what counts as "a fingerprint", and can a broken log be cleared?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-32, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, so it blocks nothing. US-ACT-04 asks for a fingerprint before the clear, and EC-ACT-02 makes a broken chain read-only evidence. SL-32 asks for a confirmation dialog, then a strong biometric with no PIN fallback (the same bar as approvals); a phone with no fingerprint enrolled cannot clear the log from the app, and a broken chain cannot be cleared at all (Delete everything, SL-26, still erases both cases). This is stricter than Q47's erase rule because the log is the evidence of what Hermit did, and a clear keeps the rest of the data. Options to ask: strong fingerprint only, no clear while the chain is broken (recommended, built) / fingerprint or the phone's PIN, like the erase (Q47) / allow clearing a broken chain too, with the clear entry recording that the old chain was broken.

## Night shift and the morning briefing (logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24)
- **Q65 At what heat does the night shift pause?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice. NFR-04 says "above the platform's moderate thermal status". Built: Android's moderate status itself already pauses (`THERMAL_PAUSE_STATUS = 2`), and a reading that fails counts as hot, so Hermit never pushes a warm phone toward severe. Options to ask: pause at moderate (recommended, built; fewer nights finish on a phone that warms while charging) / pause only above moderate, at severe (more nights finish; the phone runs warmer) / pause on Android's thermal headroom forecast (it predicts throttling before it happens, Android 11 and later only).
- **Q66 May the night shift do local writes on its own?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice. FR-CAGE-02 lets an untainted unattended session run a local write (a reminder, a note) without asking. Built: the night shift runs only reads; every other step, local writes included, is a suggestion for the morning, and a payment or a password is a refusal. Options to ask: reads only, everything else waits for the morning (recommended, built) / allow untainted local writes at night, as the cage already permits / no suggestions except reply drafts.
- **Q67 Email at night: on by default, and is the switch the permission?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice. By day every mail read asks (the `network` risk, Q42 still open), so with no one present the night shift could never read mail. Built: the email job is off by default; turning it on in HM-NIGHT-01 is the user's standing permission for exactly one read at night, unread mail (`mail_list`), never search or opening a message; by day nothing changes. Options to ask: off by default, the switch is the permission (recommended, built) / on by default once a mail account is connected / ask through a notification on the first night.
- **Q68 Which email gets a suggested reply, and what does it contain?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice. US-MAIL-07 says replies the night suggests wait for approval. Built: for unread email from people the user wrote to before (the address book, FR-MAIL-04), at most 3, code proposes an empty reply draft to that sender (`mail_draft`, a remote write); in the morning Review opens the normal sheet, the draft is saved only once approved, and sending it from HM-MAIL-04 asks again with the fingerprint. A stranger's email, including any that tells Hermit to forward or pay, gets no suggestion. Options to ask: empty drafts for known senders only (recommended, built; the email's text can't shape anything) / let the model write the draft's text in the morning from the user's words only / no reply suggestions, a "Reply" link that opens the chat instead.
- **Q69 How the night shift is woken on the phone.** RESOLVED 2026-11-14: **WorkManager with a charging constraint wakes Hermit and starts a foreground service that runs the night shift.** Built: a periodic WorkManager job every 15 minutes while charging (`apps/mobile/modules/hermit-night`), gated natively to the night window plus a 60 minute grace that closes the night; inside the gate it starts `NightService` (type `dataSync`, a small ongoing notice), which runs the headless task `HermitNightShift` (`apps/mobile/src/night-task.ts`): it opens the encrypted database and the runtime, runs one wake with the same guards and exits. A run lock in the database (`createNightLock`, `packages/night/src/lock.ts`) keeps the headless task, the in-app timer and "run now" to one pass; the in-app timer now wakes only while the app is alive and background scheduling isn't active. The schedule follows the saved settings (save, launch, after each pass) and a boot receiver re-enqueues it. Delete everything (SL-26) stops it first: a pass in flight aborts before its next write, and the erase cancels the schedule, stops the service and deletes its native preferences. Android 12 and later refuse a foreground service started from the background unless battery optimization is off for the app; then the pass runs inside the worker (ten minute limit), the refusal is recorded and HM-NIGHT-01 says so and offers the battery settings, never requiring them (Q75). Previous options: a foreground service started by WorkManager with the charging constraint (recommended, chosen) / an exact alarm at the window's start that starts the foreground service / keep the in-app timer and ask the user to leave Hermit open.
- **Q70 What a suggestion keeps to find its email after a restart.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-24, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice. Mail short ids ("m3") live only in memory. Built: a suggestion stores a snapshot of the email's header in the encrypted briefing, and the app restores it to a fresh short id before the sheet; without a snapshot the suggestion shows "No longer available". The app's `mailNight.snapshot` should keep only the provider id, account, sender, subject and time, never the preview. Options to ask: the header without the preview (recommended) / the provider id and account only, fetching the header again in the morning (one more mail read, which asks) / drop email suggestions after a restart.
- **Q75 When Android refuses the night shift's foreground service, may the worker run the pass itself?** Logged 2026-11-14 from the Q69 build, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, so it blocks nothing. Android 12 and later refuse to start a foreground service from the background unless battery optimization is off for the app (WorkManager is not an exemption), and optimization is on by default. Built: the worker catches the refusal, records it, and runs the same headless pass inside itself under WorkManager's ten minute limit with no ongoing notice; a longer night continues on the next wake, since every job's progress is saved. HM-NIGHT-01 says Android limited it and offers the battery settings, never required. Options to ask: run the pass in the worker when refused, offer the battery settings (recommended, built; most nights still finish with default settings) / skip that wake and only tell the user, so every night pass shows the notice / ask for the battery exemption during setup with Android's prompt (needs a policy justification on Google Play).

- **Q79 Where does the user approve an autofill fill?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-20, not yet asked; SL-35 (2026-11-15) built the recommended option for profile forms (HM-FORM-01, the cage decides, the native module hands the approved values back), so SL-36 follows it for logins. The spike asks there with a native fingerprint prompt (strong biometric only, the origin as the subtitle) and returns a fixed test login. US-FORM-01 wants each field and value shown on HM-FORM-01 first, and FR-CAGE-02 makes a login a `credential` risk that the cage decides and logs. - **Q80 Reading the signing certificate of the app being filled.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-20, not yet asked; a phone check decides whether it is needed. The exact-origin rule binds app logins to `android://<cert>@<package>`, so the service reads the requester's certificate from PackageManager, which Android 11 and later filter by package visibility. The browsers are declared in `<queries>`; if Android does not show the app being filled to its autofill service, every native app is refused (`no_signing_cert`, fail closed). Options to ask: if the phone check shows the certificate, nothing to add (recommended, the first thing to try) / declare `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` (Google Play allows it for password managers and autofill, with a declaration in the Play Console) / web logins only in V1, apps in V1.1.
- **Q81 Which browsers Hermit believes about the web page, and how the list is kept.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-20, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, and SL-35's profile fills use the same list. A browser's reported web domain is trusted only when its package and signing certificate are on the allowlist; any other app showing a page counts as that app. Built: the release builds of Chrome, Samsung Internet and Firefox from Google's Credential Manager privileged apps list, read 2026-11-14 and checked by tests in TypeScript and Kotlin. Options to ask: those three, updated by hand when Google's list changes (recommended, built) / ship every browser on Google's list (Brave, Edge, DuckDuckGo, Opera and more) / let the user add a browser from the vault screen behind a warning.
## MCP servers (logged 2026-11-14 from SL-51, `docs/research/mcp-client-spike.md`)
- **Q76 Accept a client secret that a server issues to this one phone?** Logged 2026-11-14, not yet asked; blocks Supabase and Figma in SL-54, nothing else. Supabase's and Figma's MCP servers register clients dynamically but only as confidential clients: each registration returns its own `client_secret`. That secret is unique to the phone that registered, not an app-wide secret shipped in the APK. Today the client refuses these servers (`needs_client_secret`) because the credential store has no field for a client secret. Options to ask: accept a per-install secret, kept in the Keystore credential store next to the tokens and never logged (recommended: two more official servers work from the phone, and the secret proves nothing beyond this install) / keep refusing and send these servers to a relay (no new secret on the phone, but the user's traffic goes through a relay) / keep refusing and say the service isn't supported yet (simplest, but two popular services stay out). SL-54 (2026-11-15), until this is decided: these servers stay refused (`needs_client_secret`), with no secret storage.
- **Q77 Which redirect does Hermit register with MCP servers, and should it host a client metadata document?** Logged 2026-11-14, not yet asked; blocks SL-54's sign-in. FR-CONN-03 says app-link redirect, but `hermit.dojocoding.io` does not resolve, so app links can't be verified on the phone today. The custom scheme `hermit://oauth/mcp` works with no domain, and the SDK reference server accepts it. Notion, Linear, Sentry, Vercel and Canva also accept a client ID that is an HTTPS URL to a static JSON document, which avoids a registration per phone. Options to ask: `hermit://oauth/mcp` with dynamic registration now, then the app link and a static client metadata document once `hermit.dojocoding.io` serves `assetlinks.json` (recommended: works today and moves to the stronger redirect without a code change) / app links only, and set up the domain before SL-54 (stronger redirect binding, but blocked on the domain) / the custom scheme only, with no client metadata document (no domain to run, but every phone registers a new client on every server). SL-54 (2026-11-15) builds the recommended option's first half: `hermit://oauth/mcp` (`MCP_REDIRECT_URI`) with dynamic registration; no client metadata document yet.
- **Q78 How much of a server's tool description reaches the model?** Logged 2026-11-14, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. The model needs some description to choose a tool, but descriptions are the server's text: the reference server's "read the user's passwords" line reaches the menu cleaned up, but its words are still there. Risk classes and the approval sheet stop the harmful calls, but a description can still steer which tool the model picks. Options to ask: the menu shows the description as one line, cleaned of markup and invisible characters, capped at 300 characters and labeled as untrusted with its host (recommended, built) / the menu shows only the tool name and a one-line note the user writes or approves at install (no server text reaches the model, more work for the user) / the description is kept, but any session with an MCP tool on the menu starts tainted (strongest, but it blocks other sends in that session until the user approves them). SL-54 (2026-11-15) ships it: the menu line is `mcpMenuLine`, and routing never reads the description.
- **Q93 Which MCP tools reach the model when the user's words name none of them?** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-54, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. At most three MCP tools reach the model per turn (`MAX_MCP_TOOLS_PER_TURN`), so the 0.8B model's menu stays small. Tools whose name or server host shares a word with the user's words come first; routing never reads a description, which is the server's text. Built: when nothing matches, the remaining slots go to the most recently used enabled tools, then install order. Options to ask: fill with the most recently used tools (recommended, built: an added server is reachable without naming it; the cage asks before every call anyway) / offer no MCP tool unless the user's words name the tool or the server (smallest menu, but the user must say "Notion" or "forecast") / let the user pin up to three tools that are always offered (predictable, one more setting).
- **Q94 Should approving one MCP read remember the server for the session?** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-54, not yet asked; built with the conservative choice, blocks nothing. A read tool the user confirmed as read-only has the `network` risk; the cage remembers approved domains only for calls with a `url`, so today every MCP read asks, every time. Options to ask: ask every time (recommended, built: an MCP read still sends the model's arguments to someone else's server) / remember the server for the session after one approved read, like read_web's domains (fewer sheets, but a tainted session could then send data out in a read's arguments without asking; the taint rule for fetches would need an MCP version) / let the user mark a tool "always allowed" on HM-CONN-03 (fewest sheets, the most trust in the server).
- **Q95 Does Delete everything revoke MCP tokens at the servers?** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-54, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. Removing one server deletes its token on the phone and then revokes it at the server (RFC 7009) where the server supports it. Built: Delete everything deletes every stored token on the phone (the `credentials` step) with no network, so the erase works offline and never waits on a server; tokens stay valid at the servers until they expire. Options to ask: delete on the phone only (recommended, built: the erase can't fail or hang on a server) / try to revoke each token first with a short timeout, then delete (the server forgets the phone too, but the erase needs the network and is slower) / delete first, then revoke in the background if the network is up (both, but work runs after the user was told everything is gone).

## Vault (logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33)
- **Q82 How long a copied password stays on the clipboard.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. Built: the clip is marked sensitive (Android 13 and later hide it from the preview and keyboard suggestions) and a native timer clears it after 30 s (`VAULT_CLIPBOARD_CLEAR_MS`) unless something else was copied since. Lock now, the app lock, the idle lock, leaving a vault screen inside Hermit and Delete everything clear it at once; going to another app does not, because that is where the user pastes it. If Android kills Hermit first, Android's own expiry is the backstop. Options to ask: 30 s, kept across the trip to another app (recommended, built) / 60 s, for slow sign-in forms / clear on every lock, including going to another app (safer, but copy then can't be used to paste anywhere outside Hermit).
- **Q83 How long the vault stays unlocked without use.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. Built: 2 minutes (`VAULT_IDLE_MS`), plus locking at once when Hermit goes to the background and when the app lock engages. Every reveal, copy and save asks for a fingerprint anyway (Q86), so the idle time only controls how long names and websites stay listed. Options to ask: 2 minutes (recommended, built) / 5 minutes / lock only when Hermit leaves the screen.
- **Q84 Only https websites in the vault.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. Built: an http address is refused with its own message, so a login is never stored for (and later filled into) an unencrypted page; that refuses logins for http intranet pages and routers. Stored origins use autofill's canonical form (`normalizeOrigin`, SL-20), which also accepts http, so allowing it later is a one-line change. Options to ask: https only (recommended, built) / allow http with a warning on the item / allow http only for private network addresses.
- **Q85 New fingerprints make the vault unreadable.** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. The Keystore key is invalidated when a fingerprint is added or removed (Android's default for biometric-bound keys), so every saved login becomes unreadable by anyone, the user included. Built: HM-VAULT-01 says so and offers Start over (a confirmed wipe and a fresh key). Options to ask: keep invalidation, offer Start over (recommended, built; someone who adds their own finger to a stolen unlocked phone gets nothing) / keep the key valid across new fingerprints (`setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(false)`, needs a small Kotlin wrapper instead of SecureStore) / add an export so the user can back up before changing fingerprints (needs a format and its own risks; SL-34 is import only).
- **Q86 A fingerprint for every reveal, copy and save, or one per unlock?** Logged 2026-11-14 from SL-33, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. US-VAULT-02 asks a fingerprint to view a secret. Built: the vault key is unwrapped for each operation and zeroed right after, so unlocking lists names and websites, and each reveal, copy and save is its own fingerprint (editing is two: one to load, one to save). Options to ask: a fingerprint per operation (recommended, built; the key is never held in the app's memory) / one fingerprint per unlock, the key held until the vault locks (fewer prompts) / per operation for reveal and copy, saves allowed for 2 minutes after one.
- **Q87 What an imported row that duplicates a saved login does by default, and how the import is logged.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-34, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. A duplicate is a row that shares an exact origin with a saved login (usernames of saved logins are sealed, so comparing them would need a second fingerprint before the preview). Built: each duplicate lists the saved login and offers Keep saved (the default), Replace (only when exactly one login matches; it keeps that login's id) or Keep both; the same login twice in the file is imported once. The signed log gets one `vault.imported` entry with the counts (added, replaced, skipped, refused) and a hash of the written items' hashes, no per-item entries. Options to ask: keep saved by default, one summary entry (recommended, built; an import never overwrites anything unless the user picks Replace) / replace by default (the file is newer, but a stale export can silently overwrite a changed password) / also log one `vault.added` or `vault.edited` entry per item by its id hash (a full trail, but thousands of signed entries for a large import).
- **Q88 How big an imported CSV may be.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-34, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. Built: 2 MiB and 5,000 logins (`IMPORT_LIMITS`), checked natively before reading, during the read and while parsing, so a huge file never sits in memory. A typical export is about 150 bytes per login, so 2 MiB is about ten thousand logins and the row cap binds first. Options to ask: 2 MiB and 5,000 logins (recommended, built) / 10 MiB and 20,000 logins (rare power users, more memory on low-end phones) / 512 KiB and 2,000 logins (tighter, may refuse a long-time Chrome user's export).
- **Q89 What happens with a CSV whose columns Hermit doesn't recognize, and Samsung Pass.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-34, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. Built: exports from Chrome and Google Password Manager, Firefox, Bitwarden and 1Password are recognized by their header, and any header that names a website column and a password column under common names (url, website, uri, password, username, login, email, notes and the like); anything else is refused with the list of supported exports, and a first row that looks like data is never taken as column names. Samsung Pass has no format of its own here: no Samsung Pass CSV export was available to check against, so it is read only if its header names a website and a password column (to check on the S26 Ultra). Options to ask: refuse unknown headers (recommended, built; a column-mapping screen would show the file's first row, which in a file without a header is a real login with its password) / add a mapping screen that shows column numbers only, never the header text / add a mapping screen with the header text behind a warning.

## Keystore-signed approvals (logged 2026-11-15 from SL-37)
- **Q96 Key attestation for the approval key.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-37, not yet asked; built with the recommended option for testnet, blocks leaving testnet. The packet doesn't ask for attestation. Built: the native module refuses a software key at enrollment and on every use (KeyInfo security level must be StrongBox or the TEE, user authentication per use, invalidated by new fingerprints), and the cage trusts only the public key pinned at enrollment after a fresh fingerprint signs a random challenge. Without attestation, a fully compromised app could in principle pin a key it made itself; attestation proves the key was made by the phone's secure hardware with these settings. Options to ask: no attestation while payments are testnet only, add it before any mainnet payment (recommended, built) / capture the attestation certificate chain at enrollment and verify it on the phone against Google's pinned attestation roots now / capture the chain and keep it in the signed log for later audit, without verifying.
- **Q97 A screen ID for the approval key screen.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-37, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. The packet names only HM-APPR-01, but losing the key (new fingerprints) needs a clear screen to set it up again. Built: a page under HM-APPR-01's ids (`HM-APPR-01.key.*`, route `/approval-key`), reached from Settings and from the blocked chat row. Options to ask: keep it under HM-APPR-01 (recommended, built, no inventory change) / add HM-APPR-03 "Approval key" to the screen inventory / fold it into HM-SET-01 as a row with its states inline.
- **Q98 Who opens spend and credential in the default rules.** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-37, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. The cage now asks for a Keystore-signed approval for spend and credential whenever the rules let them through, and denies them in tainted or unattended sessions; the default rules still floor both to "not available yet", because no payment or password skill exists until SL-40, SL-41 and the vault fill. Options to ask: each slice that ships a spend or credential skill replaces its floor rule with an ask rule (recommended, built) / open both floors now, since the cage already requires the signature / open them only behind a setting the user turns on.
## Filling forms and logging in, in other apps (logged 2026-11-15 from SL-35, and 2026-11-17 from SL-36)
- **Q90 Does filling plain profile fields need a fingerprint?** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-35, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. US-FORM-03 asks a fingerprint for sensitive fields only. Built: every fill is a `fill_form` call the cage decides and logs (Q79); a fill of plain fields (name, email, address) is approved with a tap on HM-FORM-01 after the user sees each field and value, and a fill with any sensitive field asks for the vault's strong-biometric fingerprint. With nobody on screen the cage denies every fill. Options to ask: a tap for plain fields, the fingerprint when any field is sensitive (recommended, built; the preview is the check, and the fingerprint guards what is sealed) / a fingerprint for every fill, like a send (stronger, one more prompt on every form) / a tap for every fill, the fingerprint only for ID numbers (fewer prompts, but a field the user marked sensitive fills without one).
- **Q91 Which profile fields are sensitive by default?** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-35, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. Built: ID number, tax ID and passport number are always sensitive (sealed with the vault key, never shown again, the switch locked on); every other field is plain unless the user marks it sensitive on HM-FORM-02, birth date included. A sensitive field needs the vault to exist. Options to ask: ID numbers always, the rest the user's choice (recommended, built) / also birth date and phone sensitive by default / every field sensitive (every fill asks the fingerprint, and no value is ever shown on HM-FORM-02).
- **Q92 Filling a page that isn't secure (http).** Logged 2026-11-15 from SL-35, not yet asked; built with the recommended option. The exact-origin rule identifies http pages as well as https ones (Android reports the scheme). Built: plain fields may fill into an http page, with HM-FORM-01 saying the page isn't secure; sensitive fields are never offered or filled there and are listed as held back. Options to ask: plain fields with the warning, sensitive ones never (recommended, built) / nothing at all on http, the same line as the https-only vault (Q84) / sensitive fields too, after an extra confirmation.
- **Q112 Two fingerprints for a login.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-36, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. A login is a `credential`: the cage asks for one signature by the approval key (SL-37), whose Keystore key needs a strong biometric for every use; the login's username and password are sealed with the vault key (SL-33), which also needs its own strong biometric for every unwrap (Q86). They are two Keystore keys, and one system prompt unlocks one key. Built: two prompts on HM-APPR-01, the approval key's first (its system prompt shows the site or app and the browser from the signed payload; the cage verifies the signature), then the vault's, which opens the login; a cancelled vault prompt has already spent the signature, so the next try asks both again. Options to ask: two prompts, approval then vault (recommended, built; each key keeps its per-use guarantee and nothing changes in SL-33 or SL-37) / one prompt: the vault key accepts a short window (about 10 s) after the approval prompt (fewer prompts, but the vault key is then usable without a fresh fingerprint for those seconds, and it needs a Kotlin key wrapper instead of SecureStore) / one prompt: the approval module also holds the vault key and opens the login inside the same prompt (fewest prompts, the largest native change, and it couples the two keys).
- **Q113 How an app's login gets the app's identity.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-36, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing for websites. A login is offered to an app only when the item stores the app's exact identity, `android://<cert>@<package>` (the SHA-256 of its signing key and its package); a package name alone is never an identity. Built: the vault accepts that exact form typed or pasted on HM-VAULT-02 (HM-FORM-01 and the autofill debug screen show it) and nothing looser: Chrome exports' `android://` entries (a different hash) and Bitwarden's `androidapp://` stay refused at import. Options to ask: the exact identity, pasted (recommended, built; never guessed, works today, but only power users will find it) / when an app asks and no login matches, HM-APPR-01 offers "Use a saved login for this app": the user picks one, confirms with a fingerprint, and Hermit adds the app's verified identity to it (easy for everyone, a new flow to build and review) / Digital Asset Links: a website's login also serves the apps that site lists in its `assetlinks.json` (no user step, but a network fetch per site behind an approval, and V1 sends web logins to no app).
- **Q114 What Hermit's login suggestion shows in the other app.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-36, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. Built: one suggestion per saved login for that exact origin (at most five), titled "Log in with Hermit: <login name>", so the user can choose between accounts; Android's dropdown and the keyboard's inline chip show that title, so the keyboard app sees the login's name (never the username or the password). Options to ask: the login's name (recommended, built; needed to choose an account, and FR-VAULT-02 already treats names as non-secret) / one generic "Log in with Hermit" suggestion, the account chosen on HM-APPR-01 (the keyboard sees nothing, one more step when there are several accounts) / the name in the dropdown, a generic title in the keyboard's chip.

- **Q99 GitHub Actions budget.** Resolved 2026-11-17: merge on local checks only (package tests, typecheck, app node tests) until CI runs again; Kotlin modules stay unverified meanwhile. Logged 2026-11-17; blocks every merge, because the rule is to merge only after CI is green. The Android APK job for PR #74 was refused with "The job was not started because an Actions budget is preventing further use." Options to ask: raise the DojoCodingLabs Actions budget (recommended) / run CI on a self-hosted runner on the Mac (uses the shared Mac, heavy APK builds) / merge on local package checks only until the budget resets (breaks the CI-green rule). ## Device floor and model updates (logged 2026-11-17 from SL-43)
- **Q103 The floor's numbers and what each reason allows.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-43, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. NFR-05 says Android 13 or later, arm64 and at least 8 GB; Android reports an 8 GB phone as 7.2 to 7.9 billion bytes, so the packet has no number for what Android reports. PDR-025 lets a phone below the floor run the model anyway with a warning, but some reasons make the model unable to run at all. Built (`FLOOR` in `packages/model/src/floor.ts`): below the floor under 7.0 billion bytes reported, before API 33, without arm64-v8a, without dot product, or on an Android Go phone; not arm64 and Android before 13 offer no download, the others offer "Download anyway" with the slowness warning; a fact the phone can't report never blocks; a calibration under 10 tok/s and phones QVAC forces onto the CPU (Pixel, Tensor) only warn, never block, since one slow moment can be memory pressure. Forms mode (PDR-025) is not built in this slice. Options to ask: these numbers, hard block only for arm64 and Android version (recommended, built) / hard block for every reason, no opt-in (simpler, contradicts PDR-025) / a lower memory floor (6 GB, 5.5 billion bytes reported), since the 0.8B model runs on the "low" tier of the runtime plan.
- **Q104 Where a signed model manifest comes from, and which key signs it.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-43, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks turning model updates on. US-MODEL-04 and FR-MODEL-02 say a new model arrives only with an app update that pins its hash; the wave brief asked for an Ed25519-signed manifest, and the packet names no key (Q43's Dojo key signs connector specs). Built: the manifest check (signature over the exact bytes, shape, pinned Hugging Face URL, minimum app version, no downgrade without a revocation) and the whole update machine, with `MODEL_UPDATE_SOURCE` unset in `apps/mobile/src/adapters/model-update.ts`, so this build fetches nothing, keeps no journal or pointer, and loads the pinned model exactly as before. Options to ask: keep FR-MODEL-02, a new model ships with an app release, and a separate Dojo model-signing Ed25519 key (kept off the repository, like the release key) signs a manifest the release pins (recommended, built off) / a signed manifest on a Dojo host, fetched through countedFetch, so a model can change without an app release (amends FR-MODEL-02; needs the host and the key) / no manifest, the build's pinned hash only (no revocation, no remote rollback).
- **Q105 When an update may run.** Logged 2026-11-17 from SL-43, not yet asked; built with the recommended option, blocks nothing. The packet asks for no thresholds. Built (`canUpdateNow` and `UPDATE_BATTERY_MIN` in `packages/model/src/update.ts`): never during a turn (a completion running or one ended in the last 10 s), not offline, not on metered data (cellular; expo-network can't tell a metered Wi-Fi apart), not under 30% battery off the charger, and only with room for the new file next to the old one plus the 500 MB margin; "Update now" on HM-CHAT-02 lifts the data and battery holds, never the turn or the space; the self-test loads the new file and must answer "Reply with one word: ready" with any visible text in at most 16 tokens.
